name: Apres Cyber Slopes Summit
summary: This is the Discord home for the Apres-Cyber Slopes Summit, a small ski-town themed cybersecurity conference. Members use it to discuss the event, coordinate around the in-person gathering, and chat about general security topics between events. It suits people already interested in attending or who have attended a past Slopes Summit rather than newcomers looking for a general learning community.

name: BalCCon2k26
summary: BalCCon (Balkan Computer Congress) is a non-commercial, community-organized hacker conference held annually in Novi Sad, Serbia, run entirely by volunteers from the regional hacker community. The Discord is used to discuss talks and workshops (chosen through an open call for papers), coordinate the event, and keep the Balkan hacker/maker community connected year-round. It suits anyone interested in the Balkan hacking scene, from curious beginners to experienced researchers presenting talks.

name: BSidesSLC
summary: BSidesSLC is a community-run, grassroots cybersecurity conference held in the Salt Lake City area (Sandy, Utah), with the tagline "For the People, By the People," and this Discord is also linked to sister events BSidesCache and BSidesRedRocks. People use it to talk about the annual conference's talks, hands-on workshops, and CTF contests, and to network with local security professionals year-round. It's a good fit for both newcomers curious about the field and working professionals in the Utah infosec scene.

name: BSides Charlotte
summary: This server is the shared home for two annual Charlotte, NC-area events, BSides Charlotte and FrostCon, both focused on cybersecurity education and community building. Members discuss talks, workshops, and logistics for the events and use the space to network with the local infosec community between conferences. It suits both newcomers wanting to break into security in the Charlotte region and established professionals.

name: BSides Columbus
run_by: BSides Columbus organizers (with GuidePoint Security support)
summary: BSides Columbus is an annual cybersecurity conference in Columbus, Ohio presented with support from GuidePoint Security and community sponsors, featuring talks, workshops, and hacking villages. The Discord is where attendees and local security folks discuss the event and stay connected with the Columbus infosec community year-round. It works for both beginners curious about the field and working professionals in the area.

name: BSides CT
summary: BSides CT is an all-volunteer, community-run cybersecurity conference held annually at Fairfield University in Connecticut and running since 2011. The event features talks, workshops, hands-on demos, and a CTF competition, and explicitly welcomes speakers of all experience levels; the Discord is used to plan the event and keep the Connecticut infosec community connected between conferences. It suits students and newcomers as well as established local security professionals.

name: DCG937
summary: This is the year-round Discord for DEF CON Group 937 and BSides Dayton, a volunteer-run Dayton, Ohio infosec community that hosts local meetups plus the annual BSidesDayton conference (talks, villages, and a story-driven CTF). It suits anyone in the Dayton area who wants ongoing security chat and in-person events, not just conference-week visitors.

name: BSidesDFW
summary: Run by the volunteer, 501(c)(3) nonprofit behind BSides DFW, a free annual security "unconference" in the Dallas-Fort Worth area (typically the first Saturday in November). The Discord is the year-round hub for the local community around the event, with talk announcements, CTF chatter, and general security discussion for professionals and newcomers alike.

name: Summit City Infosec
run_by: Summit City Infosec / BSides Fort Wayne volunteers
summary: Summit City Infosec is the community group behind BSides Fort Wayne, Indiana, running local security meetups and an annual BSides conference for the region. The Discord serves as a year-round gathering spot for area security folks to chat, plan meetups, and coordinate around the conference, welcoming both beginners and working professionals.

name: Houston BSides
summary: This is the Discord for BSides Houston, the Houston-area chapter of the volunteer-run global BSides security conference series. It's a smaller, moderately active space for local infosec folks to chat and connect around the annual event, useful mainly for people in or visiting the Houston area.

name: BSides Leeds
summary: BSides Leeds is a UK security conference held in Leeds (next edition June 2027 at Cloth Hall Court), explicitly welcoming newcomers through industry veterans with talks, an AMA desk, and a badge challenge. The Discord is the community's ongoing chat space for attendees and locals, sponsored in part by companies like PortSwigger.

name: BSides Memphis
summary: BSides Memphis is a 501(c)3 nonprofit, community-powered cybersecurity conference held annually in Memphis (next on October 3, 2026 at Epicenter Memphis). This is its small but active Discord for local networking and event chatter, suited to security professionals and enthusiasts in the Memphis area.

name: BSidesMKE
summary: This is the Discord for BSidesMKE, the community-run BSides security conference in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Members use it to coordinate around the yearly event (CFP, volunteering, sponsorships) and chat about local infosec between conferences. It suits anyone in the Milwaukee-area security community, from students to working professionals.

name: Security BSides Prague
summary: This is the Discord community tied to BSides Prague, a community-run BSides security conference in the Czech Republic. It's used mainly to coordinate and chat around the annual event and connect with the local Czech/Central European infosec scene. It suits security people in or visiting the region, at any experience level.

name: BSidesRoc
summary: This is the official Discord for BSidesROC, the volunteer-run BSides security conference held annually near Rochester, NY (RIT Inn & Conference Center). People use it to follow CFP/volunteer/sponsor announcements, plan meetups, and talk security year-round with the local upstate-NY community. Good fit for students and professionals in the Rochester/Western NY area.

name: BSides St Pete
summary: This is the Discord for BSides St. Pete, a community-driven cybersecurity conference on Florida's Gulf Coast run by the nonprofit Cyber Ohana Project. It draws 600+ attendees for talks and hands-on trainings each year, and members use the server to coordinate around the event, network, and talk shop with the Tampa Bay-area security community. Suitable for beginners through advanced practitioners.

name: BSides Tampa
summary: This is the Discord for BSides Tampa, one of the larger and longer-running BSides conferences in Florida. It's the most active of the Florida BSides servers here, used for CFP/volunteer coordination, networking, and general security chat throughout the year, not just around the event. It suits anyone in the Tampa Bay security community, from students to seasoned professionals.

name: BSides SWFL
summary: This is the Discord for BSides SWFL, a newer cybersecurity conference held at Florida SouthWestern State College that brings together industry professionals and students in Southwest Florida. It's a small, young community used for event coordination and local networking rather than heavy daily chat. Good fit for students and early-career people in the SWFL region.

name: CactusCon Community
summary: This is the community server for CactusCon, a long-running (14+ years) volunteer-run hacker/security conference held each February in the Phoenix, Arizona area (Mesa). Members discuss the conference CFP, talks, and villages, and use the server to stay connected between events; it welcomes newcomers alongside working security professionals.

name: secwest.net
summary: This is the community server for CanSecWest (secwest.net), a long-running, research-heavy security conference held annually in Vancouver, Canada, run by dragostech.com inc. (which also runs PACSEC and the Pwn2Own contest lineage). It skews toward vulnerability researchers, reverse engineers, and offensive security professionals rather than beginners.

name: CarolinaCon
summary: This is the community server for CarolinaCon, a long-running, community/volunteer-run hacker and security conference held in North Carolina. Members use it to discuss talks, CFP, and villages and to stay in touch with the regional hacker scene between events.

name: CornCon
summary: This is the community server for CornCon, an annual cybersecurity conference in the Quad Cities area run by the nonprofit Docent, notable for pairing an industry/CISO track with youth-focused programs like a High School Cyber Career Day and Kids' Hacker Camp. It's a friendly, community-oriented space suited to students, career-changers, and working security professionals alike.

name: CypherCon
summary: This is the community server for CypherCon, Wisconsin's largest cybersecurity and hacker conference, held each spring in Milwaukee. It covers a broad mix of security, hardware hacking, cryptography, and AI topics and explicitly aims to serve everyone from curious beginners to seasoned professionals.

name: DEFCON
run_by: DEF CON Communications, Inc. (Jeff Moss / "The Dark Tangent")
summary: This is the official, verified Discord server for DEF CON, the world's largest hacker conference, founded by Jeff Moss (The Dark Tangent) and run with an army of volunteer "Goons." It's a massive, year-round hub covering every DEF CON village and group, CTFs, and general hacker culture, with channels and communities ranging from total beginners to elite researchers.

name: Pacific Hackers
summary: Pacific Hackers Association is a Bay Area nonprofit hacker community that runs monthly meetups, the HackTheBay hackathon/CTF, and its own small conferences (PHACK, SunSecCon), plus a presence at RSA Conference. It suits people in or near San Francisco who want in-person meetups, mentorship, and hands-on CTF practice rather than just online chat.

name: Hardwear.io
summary: Hardwear.io is a well-known hardware security conference and training series (with editions in the Netherlands, USA, and India) focused on chip-level security, embedded systems, IoT, and side-channel/fault-injection research. The Discord is where attendees, speakers, and hardware security researchers discuss talks, CTFs, and training; it leans technical and suits people already working in embedded/hardware security more than newcomers.

name: HEXACON
run_by: Hexacon organizing committee (incl. Jean-Baptiste Bedrune, Jiska Classen, Ophir Harpaz)
summary: Hexacon is a single-track offensive-security conference in Paris built around vulnerability research and malware/exploitation topics, run by a committee of well-known infosec researchers with no corporate-sponsored talks. Its Discord is mainly for attendees and speakers of this ticket-limited (500 seats) event to coordinate and discuss deeply technical exploit-development and reverse-engineering content, not a place for beginners.

name: JawnCon
summary: JawnCon is a Philadelphia-area community security conference held at Arcadia University, covering cybersecurity, hardware hacking, AI governance, and general tech culture with CTFs, a lockpicking village, ham radio classes/exams, and a retro-tech show-and-tell. The Discord is where attendees and volunteers plan and chat between and during the yearly event, suiting locals interested in a smaller, community-run con.

name: LayerOne Conference
summary: LayerOne bills itself as Los Angeles' premier annual security conference, with talks on malware, cryptography, and ransomware alongside hands-on villages for hardware hacking, lockpicking, soldering, robotics battles, and a career village. The Discord serves attendees and volunteers coordinating around the yearly event, and welcomes students and hobbyists alongside working security researchers.

name: CyberV
summary: CyberV is a French cybersecurity association connecting students, professionals, and enthusiasts around projects and events, and it organizes the well-known leHACK conference (formerly Nuit du Hack) in Paris. The Discord hosts year-round French-language discussion, project collaboration, and event planning, suiting people in the French infosec scene from students to professionals.

name: NorthSec
summary: Official Discord for NorthSec, a major Montreal-based security conference and one of the largest CTF competitions in the world, covering pentesting, network and application security, reverse engineering, malware, and cryptography. The community discusses talks, training, and the CTF (roughly 90+ teams compete each year), and stays active year-round between events. It suits people already comfortable with offensive security concepts more than absolute beginners.

name: ComfyCon AU
run_by: ComfyCon AU volunteers (in partnership with PancakesCon)
summary: Discord for ComfyCon AU, a casual, community-run Australian infosec conference that partners with the beginner-focused PancakesCon on joint online programming. It's an explicitly low-pressure, welcoming space with talks, villages, and CTF-style activities aimed at people newer to the industry rather than seasoned specialists. Good fit for beginners in Australia/APAC time zones wanting an approachable entry point into the security community.

name: QueenCityCon
summary: Discord for QueenCityCon, a community-organized, multi-day cybersecurity conference in Cincinnati, Ohio built by industry volunteers and sponsors rather than a single company. The event runs breakout sessions, hands-on workshops, and a dedicated career village with resume help and mock interviews, and it's explicitly open to anyone curious about the field. It suits newcomers looking for a friendly regional on-ramp as well as working practitioners networking locally.

name: RVAsec
summary: This is the year-round Discord home for RVAsec, an annual Richmond, Virginia infosec conference with talks, a CTF, and lockpicking. Between conference dates the server keeps the community connected with chat and meetup coordination, so it suits people already in or near the Richmond security scene rather than pure newcomers looking for tutorials.

name: SAINTCON
summary: SAINTCON is a volunteer-run, nonprofit cybersecurity conference held every October in Provo, Utah, and this Discord is its active year-round community hub. Members discuss security topics, coordinate local meetups, and follow sub-communities like AppSec, hardware hacking, and lock picking that mirror the conference's tracks and contests.

name: SecretCon
summary: SecretCon is Minnesota's annual hacker and cybersecurity conference held in the Twin Cities each spring, covering hands-on hacking, AI security, privacy, and hardware across three speaker tracks and CTFs. This Discord is its community server, drawing security pros alongside curious builders and first-time hackers in that regional scene.

name: ShellCon Community
summary: ShellCon is an annual information security conference held in the beach cities near Los Angeles, streaming its main talks free on YouTube/Twitch while running paid hands-on workshops. This Discord is its year-round community server for attendees and speakers to keep talking shop between events.

name: Wild West Hackin' Fest
run_by: BHIS family of companies (Black Hills Information Security / Antisyphon Training / Active Countermeasures)
summary: This is the community Discord for Wild West Hackin' Fest, run by the BHIS family of companies (Black Hills Information Security, Antisyphon Training, Active Countermeasures). People discuss talks, workshops, and trainings from the conference (held in Deadwood, South Dakota) year-round, network with other attendees, and get updates on new events like the upcoming Mile High 2027 conference in Denver. It suits anyone into offensive/defensive security who enjoys BHIS's approachable, hands-on teaching style, from newcomers to veterans.

name: Blue Team Con
run_by: Blue Team Con organizers (community-run nonprofit conference)
summary: Official Discord for Blue Team Con, a Chicago-based conference focused on defenders (SOC analysts, detection engineers, incident responders). Members discuss conference talks, ask defensive-security questions, and connect with other blue-teamers between events. It's a good fit for people who want to focus specifically on defense rather than general or offensive security.
notes: Chicago, US. Appears to be a year-round community server (1348+ members). Not confirmed on official site (site returned 403 to fetch) but discord.com/invite link is directly resolvable and widely list

name: BSides Atlanta
summary: This is the official Discord for BSides Atlanta, a community-run annual security conference in Atlanta (2026 event at the Georgia Tech Hotel and Conference Center). Locals use it to discuss talks, coordinate volunteering, and network with the Atlanta infosec scene, including partner groups like Atlanta Women in Cyber. It suits anyone in or near Atlanta looking to connect with the regional security community, beginners included.
notes: Atlanta, GA, US. Link found in site nav labeled 'Discord' (shortened bit.ly URL, captured exactly as written). Likely year-round community. (This is a BSides regional conference, not a village/camp.)

name: RECON | Reality Escape Convention
summary: This is a long-running community Discord tied to REcon, a well-known reverse-engineering conference held in Montreal (with a sister event, REcon Brussels). People here discuss reverse engineering, binary exploitation, and malware analysis topics, and swap notes about the conference itself, which runs talks in both English and French. It's aimed at experienced reverse engineers and researchers rather than newcomers to security.
notes: No discord link on official recon.cx site itself; this appears to be a long-standing community-run REcon Discord (2100+ members) found via search, not confirmed on the official site. Montreal, Canada,

name: RSTCON
summary: This is described as the official Discord for RSTCON, a small hacking conference held in Savannah, Georgia. Members use it to discuss the conference and connect with the regional US security community; the server is fairly small, so activity is more modest than larger con servers. It suits people near coastal Georgia looking for a local infosec meetup community.
notes: Official rstcon.org page fetched empty/blank (could not verify on-site); invite found via search, described as the official RSTCON Discord (341 members). Savannah, GA, US hacking conference. Note: dis

name: THOTCON
summary: This is the Discord for THOTCON, a long-running nonprofit hacking conference held annually in Chicago (the venue is kept secret until the week of the event). The server is where attendees find event announcements, chat with other hackers, and keep in touch between conferences, and it suits anyone into the Chicago/Midwest hacker scene rather than pure beginners looking for structured lessons.
notes: Official site links this bit.ly shortlink labeled 'Discord' in its social/mail section. Chicago, US. | shortlink https://bit.ly/47Jd2cU -> https://discord.com/invite/FtUAWTPA8e

name: BSides312
summary: BSides312 is Chicago's community-run BSides conference (organized by the Hak4Kidz nonprofit), held the day after THOTCON so attendees can make a full con weekend of it. The Discord is where locals discuss the event, its CTF, lockpicking village, and Linux village, and stay connected with the Chicago infosec scene year-round.

name: Hackers Guild
summary: This server belongs to Hackers Guild PGH, a year-round Pittsburgh hacker community that also organizes the annual GuildCon conference. It's a hub for local meetups and event planning rather than a pure beginner-lessons server, though the guild itself is community-oriented and open to newcomers interested in the local hacking scene.
notes: Pittsburgh, US. Discord belongs to parent org Hackers Guild PGH (year-round community), which runs GuildCon; site itself returned 403 to fetch.
